hypothesis: Building on a CoreRank cross-domain mechanism bridge between ProbMoE's calibrated marginal subset routing and BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders, we prove formally why naive full-backward probabilistic replacement degrades reconstruction fidelity (active-set gradient distortion) and propose MarginProb-BatchTopK: preserving exact straight-through gradients on active top-k latents while routing scale-invariant calibrated marginal surrogate gradients exclusively to near-margin inactive latents. We benchmark 9 SAE architectures at 4x (d_sae=8,192) and 8x (d_sae=16,384) overcompleteness across two open-weight LLM families (Qwen3-1.7B L13 and SmolLM2-1.7B L12), evaluating reconstruction FVU, dead-latent collapse, live transformer causal splice CE Loss Recovered & Logit KL, 8-class probe recovery, and capacity-controlled Hungarian cross-seed matching.
